title.en: Unit cell occupancy with exact shared-site keys

summary: Verify conventional-cell atom counts and that neighbour expansion never duplicates a shared boundary site.
objective: Conventional-cell totals are exact integers and expanded blocks keep one entry per shared site.
applies_when: A crystal scene counts atoms per unit cell or shows fractional corner and face contributions.
The display expands to neighbouring cells or clips spheres at cell boundaries.
Site positions are computed by accumulating lattice steps.
intent_signals: my FCC cell counts six atoms
example_prompts: Check the atom accounting of this cubic unit cell scene.

principles: Unit-cell occupancy is an exact rational count: corner sites contribute one eighth, face sites one half, and a conventional cell totals an integer.

Shared sites are shared, so expanding to neighbouring cells must not create a second copy of a boundary site. Identity comes from an exact global integer key, never from a floating-point position and never from a coordinate that is unique only inside one cell.
Clipping or fading part of a sphere is presentation and does not change occupancy; a displayed fraction of a sphere is not a fraction of an atom in the count.
implementation: Represent sites on a global doubled lattice. For cell (i,j,k), add (2i,2j,2k) to all corner offsets in {0,2}^3; add (1,1,1) for BCC, or the six permutations of (0,1,1) and (2,1,1) for FCC face centres. Deduplicate global triples, retaining outer boundary sites. Store each per-cell fractional contribution separately as an exact rational.
Sum contributions for the conventional cell and compare with the expected integer for each structure displayed.

Expand to a two by two by two block of cells and compare the number of unique keys with counts derived independently from the geometry: a closed block spans a three by three by three grid of corner sites, so the body-centred structure has twenty-seven corners plus eight body centres and the face-centred structure has twenty-seven corners plus thirty-six face centres.
Test the merge rule with a coordinate produced by summing lattice steps in a different order, which a floating-point comparison would treat as a different site.
observable_checks: Weighted conventional-cell totals are exactly two for the body-centred structure and exactly four for the face-centred structure; a non-integer total names the contribution rule that is wrong.

The two by two by two block reports thirty-five unique displayed sites for the body-centred structure and sixty-three for the face-centred structure, while its weighted occupancy is sixteen and thirty-two atoms; a count that instead reaches the per-cell sum identifies duplicated boundary sites.
Toggling clipping or opacity changes no occupancy total.

known_limits: Ideal lattice accounting; it implies nothing about defects, thermal motion, measured radii or material properties.
Authored verification guidance; no scene was run or rendered for this record.
creative_affordances: Adapt the scenario, scale and presentation to your subject; this record fixes what must be checked, not how the scene must look.

claims.statement: A body-centred cubic unit cell contains two atoms and a face-centred cubic unit cell contains four, counting each corner atom as one eighth and each face atom as one half.
claims.scope: Ideal monatomic conventional cubic cells as described in the cited section; no defect, density or thermal claim.
